title: BatchCache surge thresholds investigation and safe rewind playbook
creator: Priya Patel
description: Summary: During a staged rollout of Optimize's batch/cache recommendation agent on 2026-02-27, a set of aggressive surge-threshold changes were applied to the BatchCache policy which produced lower token costs but caused intermittent tail-latency regressions for multi-turn chat workloads. The autotuner applied threshold expansions in the production canary zone after the metric gate passed, but a change in traffic skew (larger proportion of short-sequence calls) resulted in degraded cache hit behavior and increased KV cache churn. This ticket captures the investigation, immediate mitigations, and a formalized 'safe rewind' playbook to prevent similar regressions.
postmortem_summary: Root cause: the agent's surge-threshold expansion heuristic did not account for sudden shifts in sequence-length distribution and took effect without an isolation guard for KV cache churn. Contributing factors: (1) metric gate used median latency and cost delta rather than tail latency and stability score; (2) missing circuit-breaker for cache churn rate; (3) canary sampling window too short (15m) during a traffic shift. Impact: 12% increase in p99 latency for affected endpoints during a 90-minute window, customer-facing timeouts for two internal sandbox tenants, and temporary elevated token spend anomalies. Decision: revert aggressive thresholds, introduce cache-churn monitor and automated soft-fallback, and update rollout gating to include tail-latency and stability metrics.
mitigation_plan: 1) Immediate: roll back the batch/cache recommendations applied in the canary zone and freeze Optimize agent auto-applies for 48h. 2) Near-term: deploy a cache-churn circuit-breaker that blocks threshold increases when churn > X/s and when p95/p99 delta > configured thresholds. 3) Medium-term: expand rollout gating to include p99 latency, cache stability score, and a traffic-shift detector. 4) Long-term: add synthetic sequence-mix tests to the canary pipeline and maintain a week-long rolling baseline for sequence-length distribution.
playbook_steps: Step 0 — Triage: If p99 latency increases >10% and churn rate > threshold, notify SRE on-call and tag incident channel #optimize-incidents.

Step 1 — Immediate rewind: Use the snapshot tool to restore BatchCache config to the last-known-good snapshot (snapshot id available in artifacts). If snapshot restore fails, apply manual override: set batch_size and cache_threshold back to conservative defaults and disable autotune for the lane.
Step 2 — Circuit breaker activation: Trigger the cache-churn circuit-breaker to pause further applies; emit event to audit log and start a 15-minute observation window before automated unpause.

Step 3 — Canary hardening: Extend canary window to 90 minutes for any threshold expansion >10%; require p99 and stability score to remain within acceptance bounds for two consecutive windows before promoting.

Step 4 — Post-rollback validation: Run synthetic acceptance harness against representative short/long sequence mixes; validate p50/p95/p99 and cache hit ratio. Record results to dashboard 'Optimize/Canary/Validation'.

Step 5 — Communication: Post incident summary to #product-optimize and create a customer-facing notice template for affected tenants. Schedule a cross-team review with SRE, Runtime, and DX within 3 business days.

Step 6 — Preventative follow-ups: Add a gating rule in the autotune policy to require at least one 'stability-scan' (synthetic) and a data-shift detector prior to any apply > 5% change in batching or cache thresholds.
Step 7 — Automation safety: Add staged apply with holdback cohort and automatic rollback condition if p99 or churn worsens by configured delta within 2 windows.
Step 8 — Documentation: Write an incident playbook entry and link to confluence doc 'Optimize AutoTune Safe Rewind' and update the on-call runbook.
rollback_checklist: Verify latest stable snapshot exists for the affected model variant and zone
Notify SRE & Optimize on-call and open incident channel
Restore snapshot via config-snapshot tool with dry-run validation
If dry-run passes, execute live restore and confirm cache-hit ratio and tail latency metrics are trending back toward baseline
Close autotune apply freeze and record change in audit log with reason
Create follow-up tickets for instrumentation gaps identified during rollback
